title: NLAS-multi: A Multilingual Corpus of Automatically Generated Natural Language Argumentation Schemes
authors: Ramon Ruiz-Dolz; Joaquin Taverner; John Lawrence; Chris Reed
task_description: Identify argumentation schemes in natural-language arguments across languages and topics.
inputs: 1,893 English and 1,917 Spanish generated/curated arguments instantiated from 20 Walton schemes; the paper describes multilingual scheme instances and topic/stance variation.
outputs_or_labels: Scheme labels and scheme-family labels; baseline and fine-tuned classification results.
pipeline_gap_filled: Multilingual argument-form classification -> scheme-conditioned structure extraction
artifact_access_status: Article and supplementary resource are publicly discoverable; exact repository/download endpoint should be rechecked before deployment.
license_status: Dataset license not independently verified in this pass.
evidence_basis: DOI record and ACL-linked discussion identify 20 schemes and English/Spanish corpus sizes; local summary records classification baselines and synthetic-data caveats.
limitations: Automatically generated arguments are more templatic than human dialogue; translation/language effects are entangled with generation and validation.
why_relevant: Strongest direct multilingual argument-structure resource found; useful for cross-language scheme transfer and a controlled form layer, but must be paired with human-authored data.

title: Multi-lingual Argumentative Corpora in English, Turkish, Greek, Albanian, Croatian, Serbian, Macedonian, Bulgarian, Romanian and Arabic
authors: Adrian Aker; Yevgeni Kabadjov; Lluís Màrquez; Stefan Puscasu; Emine Yilmaz; Thomas Roelleke
task_description: Project argumentative/non-argumentative labels from English into aligned parallel corpora and evaluate multilingual argument mining.
inputs: Sentence-aligned SETimes English plus eight Balkan languages and Arabic-English Huffington Post parallel news; source-language classifier votes are projected to target sentences and a manually annotated news corpus is used for evaluation.
outputs_or_labels: Argumentative versus non-argumentative labels; per-classifier votes and majority decisions; reported F1 evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: Parallel-text argument-span/argumentative-sentence detection -> multilingual provenance alignment
artifact_access_status: ACL paper/PDF accessible; data are described as publicly available or available by request, but current download endpoint was not independently resolved.
license_status: License and redistribution terms require artifact-level verification.
evidence_basis: ACL PDF/search evidence explicitly describes aligned parallel corpora, the ten-language scope, projection method, and manual evaluation.
limitations: Labels are projected from English models rather than independently annotated in every language; sentence-level argument detection is coarser than premise/conclusion extraction.
why_relevant: Rare resource with literal parallel texts and multilingual argument labels; valuable for measuring whether structural extraction survives translation while preserving alignment.

title: LogiQA: A Challenge Dataset for Machine Reading Comprehension with Logical Reasoning
authors: Jian Liu; Leyang Cui; Hanshi Sun; Jinyang Lin; Dandan Li; Yue Zhang
task_description: Multiple-choice machine reading comprehension requiring deductive, analytical, and logical reasoning over expert-written passages.
inputs: 8,678 expert-written instances derived from Chinese civil-service examination materials; Chinese source text with answer options and reasoning types.
outputs_or_labels: Four-way answer labels and reported reasoning-type breakdowns; accuracy against human ceiling.
pipeline_gap_filled: Culturally situated deductive reasoning -> reasoning-label evaluation
artifact_access_status: Paper and public GitHub artifact are discoverable; exact data files should be pinned before use.
license_status: Repository/data license should be checked at download time.
evidence_basis: arXiv/IJCAI record and local summary state 8,678 instances, Chinese civil-service source, and deductive reasoning design.
limitations: Exam genre, language, translation, and educational conventions confound logical ability; not evidence for a unitary Chinese logic.
why_relevant: Best direct Chinese-source reasoning benchmark in the set; useful as an authentic non-English reasoning control with explicit caveats.

title: LogiQA 2.0—An Improved Dataset for Logical Reasoning in Natural Language Understanding
authors: Jian Liu; Leyang Cui; Hanmeng Liu; Dandan Li; Yue Zhang
task_description: Reannotated logical reading comprehension and natural-language inference with professionally translated English-facing material.
inputs: Expanded/reannotated Chinese-source reasoning items with professional manual translation and filtering of culturally opaque idioms; paired MRC/NLI-style task material.
outputs_or_labels: Logical answer labels, NLI labels, and reasoning-type metadata as described by the paper/dataset card.
pipeline_gap_filled: Cross-language reasoning invariance -> translation-aware deductive evaluation
artifact_access_status: DOI record and Hugging Face dataset card are accessible; artifact identity is resolved but exact revision/license should be pinned.
license_status: Dataset license/terms require verification from the current card before redistribution.
evidence_basis: DOI and dataset-card search evidence identify professional manual translation, reannotation, and the cross-lingual comparison purpose.
limitations: English normalization can remove culturally distinctive cues; inherited exam genre remains narrow and translation may still alter difficulty.
why_relevant: Useful paired resource for separating reasoning failure from translation and culture effects while retaining a Chinese-source provenance trail.

title: XCOPA: A Multilingual Dataset for Causal Commonsense Reasoning
authors: Edoardo Maria Ponti; Goran Glavaš; Olga Majewska; Qianchu Liu; Ivan Vulić; Anna Korhonen
task_description: Choose the more plausible cause or effect for a premise across aligned multilingual instances.
inputs: Human-translated and reannotated COPA validation/test items in 11 typologically diverse languages, including Haitian Creole and Eastern Apurímac Quechua; instances are aligned across languages.
outputs_or_labels: Binary plausible-alternative labels for cause/effect questions; cross-lingual transfer and language-wise accuracy.
pipeline_gap_filled: Parallel causal reasoning -> multilingual reasoning invariance and low-resource transfer
artifact_access_status: ACL page and official GitHub repository are accessible; artifact is widely mirrored but revision/license should be pinned.
license_status: Dataset license not independently verified in this pass.
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states 11 languages, typological diversity, aligned instances, and causal commonsense task; official GitHub is linked by the paper.
limitations: Translated COPA inherits English task assumptions and may not capture culture-native causal knowledge; binary labels hide explanatory structure.
why_relevant: Strong clean control for multilingual causal inference and cross-language consistency; complements argument-form resources rather than replacing them.

title: E-KAR: A Benchmark for Rationalizing Natural Language Analogical Reasoning
authors: Yinping Chen; Shao-Yen Tseng; Sijia Liu; Yue Yu; Chao Wang; Caiming Xiong; Richard Socher; Xuewei Bao
task_description: Answer analogical multiple-choice questions and produce rationalizations in two languages/source settings.
inputs: 1,655 Chinese and 1,251 English problems sourced from civil-service examinations; candidate answers and explanation annotations.
outputs_or_labels: Answer choice plus free-text rationalization; manually annotated candidate-answer/explanation quality.
pipeline_gap_filled: Cross-language analogical structure -> explanation and relational mapping evaluation
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF and official repository are accessible; exact data revision/license should be pinned.
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/search evidence identifies bilingual counts, exam provenance, QA plus rationalization tasks, and manual annotation.
limitations: Chinese and English subsets are not necessarily parallel translations; exam conventions and knowledge demands confound analogy with language/culture.
why_relevant: Direct bilingual resource for testing whether systems expose relational structure rather than only select an answer.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models with NeuBAROCO: Syllogistic Reasoning Ability and Human-like Biases
task_description: Evaluate categorical syllogism validity and human-associated reasoning biases in English and Japanese.
inputs: Psychology-derived categorical syllogism items rendered/evaluated in English and Japanese, with validity, figure, belief-bias, conversion, and atmosphere manipulations.
outputs_or_labels: Validity/entailment-style judgments and bias/error profiles; language-wise comparisons.
pipeline_gap_filled: Parallel syllogistic form -> formal reasoning and bias diagnostics
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF accessible; repository is discoverable, but exact benchmark files/license need pinning.
evidence_basis: ACL paper and local summary state English/Japanese coverage and belief-bias, conversion, and atmosphere conditions.
limitations: Translation and provenance effects can mimic reasoning differences; human-like bias is not equivalent to correct reasoning.
why_relevant: Best multilingual formal-logic control for content bias and language-preserving form comparisons; should be scored separately from cultural knowledge benchmarks.

title: Are Multilingual LLMs Culturally-Diverse Reasoners? An Empirical Study of Multilingual Proverb Understanding
task_description: Interpret proverbs and sayings in conversational situations and test cross-cultural reasoning versus memorization.
inputs: Proverbs/sayings with situational conversations in English, German, Russian, Bengali, Mandarin Chinese, and Indonesian; figurative/non-figurative annotations and translation conditions.
outputs_or_labels: Meaning interpretation, figurative-status labels, source/target-language performance, and language/culture-gap measures.
pipeline_gap_filled: Culturally embedded implicit reasoning -> pragmatic/figurative context evaluation
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF and official GitHub repository are accessible; exact release license should be checked.
evidence_basis: ACL abstract/search evidence identifies six languages, conversational inference task, figurative labels, and culture-gap analysis.
limitations: Proverb interpretation is defeasible/pragmatic rather than deductive; translation quality and cultural familiarity remain major confounds.
why_relevant: Directly tests whether multilingual models preserve culturally grounded inferential meaning under context and translation, a gap left by formal logic suites.

title: SeaEval for Multilingual Foundation Models: From Cross-Lingual Alignment to Cultural Reasoning
authors: Bin Wang; Zhengyuan Liu; Xin Huang; Fangkai Jiao; Yang Ding; AiTi Aw; Nancy Chen
task_description: Evaluate multilingual foundation models on alignment, reasoning, semantics, cultural practices, nuances, values, and cross-lingual consistency.
inputs: English, Chinese, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Malay, Filipino, and other Southeast Asian language/culture task sets; includes parallel Cross-MMLU and Cross-LogiQA subsets.
outputs_or_labels: Task accuracy, cultural reasoning scores, and consistency across semantically equivalent multilingual questions.
pipeline_gap_filled: Multilingual reasoning invariance -> cultural/translation robustness control
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF and linked repository are accessible; exact artifact version/license should be pinned.
license_status: Repository/data licensing varies by component and was not independently verified.
evidence_basis: ACL record/search evidence identifies reasoning, cultural reasoning, Cross-MMLU, and Cross-LogiQA parallel subsets in seven languages.
limitations: Broad suite mixes language proficiency, factual knowledge, culture, and reasoning; individual failures are not causally isolated.
why_relevant: High-value composite control for cross-lingual consistency and cultural framing, especially the parallel logical subset.

title: Global MMLU: Understanding and Addressing Cultural and Linguistic Biases in Multilingual Evaluation
task_description: Evaluate knowledge and reasoning across translated, culturally sensitive, and culturally agnostic subsets in 42 languages.
inputs: MMLU-derived questions translated professionally and by community, human verified, with culturally sensitive/agnostic partitions and regional/domain metadata.
outputs_or_labels: Multiple-choice answers, translation/cultural-sensitivity labels, and language-wise performance/ranking shifts.
pipeline_gap_filled: Translation-vs-content confound separation -> multilingual evaluation design
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF accessible; repository/artifact should be pinned and license checked before reuse.
license_status: Dataset license not independently verified in this pass.
evidence_basis: ACL/arXiv record and local summary state 42 languages, human verification, culturally sensitive/agnostic subsets, and translation artifacts.
limitations: MMLU remains inherited from English-centric subject design; multiple-choice scores do not expose proof or argument structure.
why_relevant: Important calibration resource for any multilingual reasoning claim; prevents treating translation coverage as cultural validity.

title: Commonsense Reasoning in Arab Culture
authors: Abdelrahman Sadallah; Junior Cedric Tonga; Khalid Almubarak; et al.
task_description: Answer culturally grounded commonsense questions authored and validated by native speakers across Arab regions.
inputs: Modern Standard Arabic questions from 13 countries, four broad regions, 12 daily-life domains, and 54 subtopics; native-speaker authoring and validation.
outputs_or_labels: Multiple-choice commonsense labels and regional/language/model performance.
pipeline_gap_filled: Native-authored cultural reasoning -> region-sensitive context evaluation
artifact_access_status: ACL paper/PDF accessible; dataset release endpoint was not independently resolved.
license_status: Dataset license/access terms not independently verified.
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly states 13-country coverage, native-speaker construction, domains/subtopics, and model evaluation.
limitations: MSA and country categories cannot represent all dialects or intra-country disagreement; single gold answers compress cultural plurality.
why_relevant: Strong Arabic-native complement to translated multilingual benchmarks and a useful test of culturally situated premise interpretation.

title: GeoMLAMA: Geo-Diverse Commonsense Probing on Multilingual Pre-Trained Language Models
authors: Da Yin; Li Dong; Shizhe Diao; et al.
task_description: Probe geographically differentiated commonsense associations in multilingual pretrained models.
inputs: 3,125 cloze prompts in English, Chinese, Hindi, Persian, and Swahili linked to American, Chinese, Indian, Iranian, and Kenyan contexts.
outputs_or_labels: Cloze completion accuracy and geographic/language/model comparisons.
pipeline_gap_filled: Cultural premise retrieval -> geo-diverse knowledge/context diagnostic
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF and repository are accessible; exact artifact license should be checked.
evidence_basis: ACL record/search evidence states five languages, 3,125 prompts, geographic contexts, and multilingual model probing.
limitations: Cloze association is not multi-step reasoning; country labels simplify within-country diversity and language accessibility.
why_relevant: Useful low-level control for culturally situated premise retrieval before interpreting failures on richer reasoning tasks.

title: Common Sense Beyond English: Evaluating and Improving Multilingual Language Models for Commonsense Reasoning
authors: Bill Yuchen Lin; Szu-Yu Lee; Yun-Nung Qiao; Yuchen Ren
task_description: Probe commonsense knowledge and reasoning beyond English and test cross-lingual transfer.
inputs: Mickey corpus with 561,000 sentences in 11 languages; multilingual probe; translated/cross-lingual CSQA and CODAH variants in 16 languages.
outputs_or_labels: Probe and multiple-choice commonsense labels; language-wise zero-shot and contrastive-pretraining results.
pipeline_gap_filled: Multilingual commonsense transfer -> language/knowledge versus reasoning separation
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF and repository are accessible; exact data license should be pinned.
license_status: Dataset and source-corpus terms were not independently verified.
evidence_basis: ACL record/local summary identify corpus size, 11/16-language coverage, and cross-lingual CSQA/CODAH evaluations.
limitations: Translated tasks inherit English assumptions and mostly test plausibility/common sense rather than argument validity or proof structure.
why_relevant: Broad multilingual baseline for measuring whether a reasoning method transfers beyond English without claiming culturally native validity.
